answer: Each agent could be required to lock a scarce token in an on-chain bond before earning reputation or receiving work. A garden of newcomers can still join, but every fake identity ties up another bond, and identities that fail audits or abandon jobs lose it. This makes a sybil attack costly in proportion to the influence it seeks: one willow of cheap wallets cannot multiply voting weight for free, while honest agents can recover their stake. An inlet for small, refundable bonds can keep entry open without removing that economic friction.
